sections.heading: Clogged Fin-Tube Bundles Are Cutting Into Your Plant's Cooling Output
paragraphs: Air coolers are the backbone of heat rejection in oil and gas, petrochemical, refining, and power plants across Thailand. Once fin surfaces start collecting dust, oil film, and oxide layers, airflow drops, and the whole unit works harder just to hold the same temperature.
Most of this fouling cannot be cleared with chemical solvents or standard abrasive blasting, since both risk stripping fin coatings or leaving harmful residue behind on sensitive surfaces.
ICST instead applies a dry soda blast cleaning process built around sodium bicarbonate, a soft, non-caustic media that lifts contamination while acting as a natural rust inhibitor for bare metal.
Keeping your ACHE bundle clean directly protects output and energy costs.
Eco-friendly, non-destructive cleaning for ACHEs, machinery, and delicate equipment.

ICST offers advanced Dry Soda Blast Cleaning Services to improve and optimize the operation of your air-cooled heat exchangers (ACHE). Our techniques support cooling efficiency, help minimize downtime, and enhance system performance.

sections.heading: What Is Soda Blasting?
paragraphs: Soda blasting uses compressed air to propel sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) particles onto surfaces, effectively removing contaminants, dirt, paint, and corrosion. Its gentle yet efficient process makes it a popular choice for cleaning delicate materials like wood, glass, and concrete, all without damaging the underlying surface.
Even better, it’s environmentally friendly. The water-soluble, non-toxic soda media leaves no harmful residues, making it an excellent green alternative to traditional abrasive cleaning methods.

sections.heading: Applications of Dry Soda Blasting
paragraphs: Soda blasting, also known as dry soda blasting or bicarbonate of soda blasting, has gained popularity in various industries due to its versatility and effectiveness. Here are some common applications of dry soda blasting:

bullets.text: Non-Destructive Cleaning: Soda blasting effectively removes dirt, grime, and contaminants without damaging the underlying material, making it ideal for delicate surfaces.
Cost-Effective Solution: This cleaning method is a budget-friendly way to restore surfaces like boat hulls and even fire-damaged areas, saving on extensive repairs or replacements.
Environmentally Friendly: Soda blasting uses non-toxic, water-soluble media, making it a sustainable and eco-conscious choice for both residential and industrial cleaning.
Versatile Application: Suitable for a variety of surfaces, including wood, glass, concrete, and metal, soda blasting can clean delicate substrates without causing corrosion or damage.
Prevents Surface Damage: The gentle yet effective nature of soda blasting preserves the integrity of surfaces, ensuring no harm is done during the cleaning process.
Industrial Cleaning: Soda blasting quickly removes grease, oil, dirt, and contaminants without harming delicate machinery or surfaces.
Automotive Restoration: soda blasting works well on classic cars, removing paint and rust while preserving the metal underneath.
Graffiti Removal: Easily clean graffiti off buildings and structures without damaging the original surface.
Mold Remediation: Removes mold and mildew while preventing regrowth, leaving surfaces clean and safe.
Fire Restoration: Clears soot and smoke damage from walls and ceilings with minimal impact, ideal for post-fire recovery.

sections.heading: How ICST's Dry Soda Blasting Process Works
paragraphs: At ICST, we go beyond just surface cleaning, our complete cleaning process ensures your equipment operates at peak efficiency. Our advanced method effectively removes impurities and debris without compromising the structural integrity of your cooling bundles.

sections.heading: Step 01 — Initial System Inspection
paragraphs: Every job starts with a visual survey of the fin-tube bundle. Our team notes fouling severity, checks the underlying surface condition, and flags any coating damage that needs attention before blasting begins.

sections.heading: Step 02 — Blasting Equipment Preparation
paragraphs: We configure the blast pot, blast hose, and soda blaster for the job at hand, selecting the right soda media grade for softer substrates such as aluminum fins. Every setup includes a moisture separator to keep the air line dry and consistent.

sections.heading: Step 03 — Precision Cleaning Control
paragraphs: Our experts watch nozzle distance and airflow throughout the job, correcting for inadequate air supply or pressure drift so soda particles clean evenly without marking delicate fin material.

sections.heading: Step 04 — Final Inspection and Site Cleanup
paragraphs: Once fouling is cleared, we run a post-blasting inspection across the bundle. Because sodium bicarbonate particles are water soluble and non-hazardous, there is no abrasive grit left behind and no risk of flash rusting on exposed metal.

sections.heading: Step 05 — Service Report and Documentation
paragraphs: ICST logs blast settings, surface condition, and before-and-after results for every job, giving your maintenance team a clear record to plan future service intervals.

sections.heading: Measurable Airflow and Thermal Gains After Every Clean
paragraphs: Our field data consistently shows improved airflow and heat transfer once a bundle has been through our dry soda blasting service. Facilities typically regain lost capacity by clearing grease film, oxide buildup, and breakdown layers left behind by older rust inhibitor coatings.

bullets.text: What is the difference between wet and dry soda blasting?

Wet soda blasting mixes water with baking soda to minimize dust and cool surfaces, making it ideal for outdoor or high-dust applications. Dry soda blasting uses only soda media with compressed air, offering better visibility and precision for indoor or sensitive environments.
What is soda blasting used for?

Soda blasting is used to clean or strip surfaces without causing damage. It’s widely applied for removing paint, oil, mold, rust, and coatings from engines, machinery, food-grade equipment, buildings, and historic structures.
What is the process of dry blasting?

In dry soda blasting, compressed air propels fine sodium bicarbonate particles at a surface to clean or strip it. The soft media breaks on impact, lifting contaminants without harming the base material — making it ideal for delicate or precision cleaning jobs.
Is soda blasting expensive?
Soda blasting is cost-effective for sensitive or detailed cleaning jobs. While it may cost more than traditional methods, it reduces the need for repairs or re-coating due to its non-damaging nature.
Is dry soda blasting safe for delicate surfaces?
Yes. Dry soda blasting is non-abrasive and safe for sensitive surfaces like stainless steel, aluminum, glass, and even food processing equipment. It cleans without scratching or etching.
How is soda blasting different from sandblasting?

Unlike sandblasting, soda blasting uses sodium bicarbonate, which is much gentler. It doesn’t generate heat, warp surfaces, or leave toxic residue, making it safer for people, equipment, and the environment.
